The shared Part II endpoint now represents the same model point for replay,
differentiation and continuation. At the retained DEA start-0 endpoint, the
maximum relative difference between differentiated and replayed predictions
falls from 0.04738229639939395 to exactly zero across 80 fitted rows. The
replay cost remains 8.03397189312541. This is numerical verification on one
Engine wheel, not physical validation or parameter adoption.

## Coordinate transport

[Issue #365](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/365)
owns this correction and its same-wheel relative identity limit of $10^{-8}$.
The scope and wheel follow the series rules in
[issue #337](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/337).
The shared owner is `Route.endpoint_mapping` in `analyses/part_ii.py`.

For a coordinate with origin $o$, scale $s$ and returned optimizer value $u$,
the fitted value is $x=o+su$. If completing the reaction law gives coefficient
$c$, the replacement origin is $c$ and both bounds are translated by $c-x$.
The fit displacement $su$ does not translate the bounds. The enthalpy shift
is already incorporated in the completed law, so its origin resets to zero
and its bounds retain the existing translation by the absorbed shift.
Applying this mapping again with zero optimizer displacement and the same
completed law leaves the endpoint unchanged. A later continuation transports
only its additional completion offset.

The old path completed the laws and reset enthalpy shifts while leaving the
reaction coefficient in the previous chart. The correction replaces that
incomplete transport in the shared owner. Endpoint reuse and continuation
consume this mapping through `stable_refit_255.stage_fit`; uncertainty
consumes its output without a separate amine correction.

## Same-wheel evidence

The [retained verification](results/verification.json) contains all DEA replay
and differentiated predictions, coordinate origins and bounds, source hashes,
and caller checks. Calculations used Engine main `391dfe5d64ede5036bf160bc6ae037ad5e14af32`,
wheel SHA-256 `0962e21d2fa7a8ba1ed4622f1110b3e8053bacd878fa41c999d85e8b9afab66b`.
`Route.verify` checked installed package bytes against that wheel.
The DEA inputs were read from the #346 task checkout; their exact input hashes
are retained. Its running campaign and branch were not modified.

| Quantity | Previous chart | Completed chart |
|---|---:|---:|
| DEA cost, dimensionless half-sum of weighted squared residuals | 8.03397189312541 | 8.03397189312541 |
| First replayed CO2 partial pressure, Pa | 2476.6125757577397 | 2476.6125757577397 |
| First differentiated CO2 partial pressure, Pa | 2359.26498462672 | 2476.6125757577397 |
| Maximum relative prediction difference, 80 rows | 0.04738229639939395 | 0 |
| Carbamate-hydrolysis coefficient a origin | 5.778214151903766 | 5.869410673201805 |
| Coefficient a lower bound | 4.097376425483943 | 4.188572946781981 |
| Coefficient a upper bound | 10.097376425483944 | 10.188572946781981 |

The bound translation is +0.09119652129803857. Repeating transport with zero
displacement gives an identical endpoint, including bounds. The regression
test also checks a nonzero continuation with an offset of opposite sign.
These few scalar identity checks use tables because a plot would add no
information about the exact equality being checked.

Existing MEA callers retain their own chart owner. Using the #340 frozen

| MEA F2 | 307 | 150.76290287953717 | 0 |
| MDEA B1, shared Part II route | 278 | 374.51907880524016 | 0 cost difference from #365's required reference |

The MEA references and parameter inputs are those named by

MDEA uses `analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/inputs/part-ii-replay.json`, with

## Conditional uncertainty and limits

On the old DEA chart, `Route.uncertainty` rejects the point with
`Differentiation/replay row mismatch` before calculating standard errors.
The corrected chart passes that same assertion. The
[conditional information](results/conditional-uncertainty.json) retains standard
errors of 0.0034855873154973523 for DEAH–water interaction,
0.054321087209096015 for DEACOO–water interaction,
0.6151039779186511 for hydrolysis a, and 1346.321881855986 J/mol for the
hydrolysis enthalpy shift. These are conditional on the fitted model,
residual scales and local linearization. No new fit, scientific assessment,
parameter adoption, or physical uncertainty claim follows from chart identity.
The regression test confirms an identity failure writes no standard-error file.
